What if all eight billion people on Earth jumped at the same time?
Together, we weigh about four hundred million tonnes.
Sounds like a lot? Earth is about fifteen trillion times heavier.
When we push off, Earth moves the other way… by less than the width of an atom.
And when we land, it moves right back. Nobody would feel a thing.
Seismometers near big crowds might pick up a tiny tremor… and that's it.
The hardest part? Getting eight billion people, in every time zone, to jump at the exact same second.
Would you join in? Tell me in the comments.
